Some scraping of the NBA API to get some defensive stats


https://www.nba.com/stats/players/defense-dash-3pt?dir=A&sort=PLAYER_NAME
```{r}
# Install these if you don't have them: install.packages(c("httr", "jsonlite"))
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)

# 1. The exact hidden API endpoint for Player Tracking Defense
url <- "https://stats.nba.com/stats/leaguedashptdefend"

# 2. Define the exact API categories and the suffixes we want to add to the columns
categories <- c("Overall", "3-Pointers", "Less Than 6 Ft", "Less Than 15 Ft", "2-Pointers")
suffixes <- c("_OVERALL", "_3P", "_LT_6", "_LT_15", "_2P")

# 2. The "Fake ID" headers (Mandatory: do not change these)
headers <- c(
  `Connection` = 'keep-alive',
  `Accept` = 'application/json, text/plain, */*',
  `User-Agent` = 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36',
  `Referer` = 'https://www.nba.com/',
  `Origin` = 'https://www.nba.com'
)

# 3. The parameters for your specific season
# Note: I set this to "2018-19" based on your earlier graph code, but change it if needed!
params <- list(
  College = "", Conference = "", Country = "", 
  DefenseCategory = "Greater Than 15Ft", # "Overall" gives DFG%. Can also be "3-Pointers" or "Less Than 6 Ft"
  DraftPick = "", DraftYear = "", Height = "", 
  LastNGames = "0", LeagueID = "00", Location = "", 
  Month = "0", OpponentTeamID = "0", Outcome = "", 
  PORound = "0", 
  PerMode = "PerGame", # Or use "Totals" / "Per100Possessions"
  PlayerPosition = "", 
  Season = "2015-16",  # <-- CHANGE THIS TO MATCH YOUR OFFENSIVE DATA
  SeasonSegment = "", SeasonType = "Regular Season", 
  TeamID = "0", Weight = ""
)

# 4. Make the request to the NBA servers
response <- GET(url, add_headers(.headers=headers), query = params)

# 5. Unpack the JSON response into a clean R dataframe
json_data <- fromJSON(content(response, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))

# The NBA buries the actual data inside a nested list. This extracts it:
col_names <- json_data$resultSets$headers[[1]]
data_rows <- json_data$resultSets$rowSet[[1]]

fifte_nba_tracking_defense <- as.data.frame(data_rows, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colnames(fifte_nba_tracking_defense) <- col_names

# 6. Clean up the variable types (everything comes in as character text)
fifte_nba_tracking_defense <- fifte_nba_tracking_defense %>%
  mutate(across(c(4:ncol(.)), as.numeric))

# Check out your new data!
head(fifte_nba_tracking_defense)
```


https://www.nba.com/stats/players/opponent-shooting?Season=2015-16&DistanceRange=By+Zone
```{r}
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)

# 1. API endpoint
url <- "https://stats.nba.com/stats/leaguedashplayershotlocations"

headers <- c(
  `Connection` = 'keep-alive',
  `Accept` = 'application/json, text/plain, */*',
  `User-Agent` = 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36',
  `Referer` = 'https://www.nba.com/',
  `Origin` = 'https://www.nba.com'
)

# 2. Parameters for Opponent Shooting By Zone
params <- list(
  College = "", Conference = "", Country = "", DateFrom = "", DateTo = "",
  DistanceRange = "By Zone", 
  Division = "", DraftPick = "", DraftYear = "", GameScope = "", GameSegment = "",
  Height = "", LastNGames = "0", LeagueID = "00", Location = "",
  MeasureType = "Opponent",  # Opponent shooting
  Month = "0", OpponentTeamID = "0", Outcome = "", PORound = "0", PaceAdjust = "N",
  PerMode = "PerGame", Period = "0", PlayerExperience = "", PlayerPosition = "",
  PlusMinus = "N", Rank = "N", Season = "2015-16", SeasonSegment = "",
  SeasonType = "Regular Season", ShotClockRange = "", StarterBench = "",
  TeamID = "0", VsConference = "", VsDivision = "", Weight = ""
)

# 3. Hit the API
print("Scraping Opponent Shooting By Zone...")
response <- GET(url, add_headers(.headers=headers), query = params)
json_data <- fromJSON(content(response, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))

# 4. THE FIX: Smart Data Extraction
# This checks if the NBA sent an array (needs [[1]]) or a direct object
if ("data.frame" %in% class(json_data$resultSets)) {
  raw_headers <- json_data$resultSets$headers[[1]]
  data_rows <- json_data$resultSets$rowSet[[1]]
} else {
  raw_headers <- json_data$resultSets$headers
  data_rows <- json_data$resultSets$rowSet
}

# 5. Smart Header Parsing
# This safely checks for the NBA's annoying "double headers"
if (is.data.frame(raw_headers) && "columnNames" %in% names(raw_headers)) {
  top_headers <- raw_headers$columnNames[[1]]
  bottom_headers <- raw_headers$columnNames[[2]]
  top_headers[top_headers == ""] <- "INFO"
  clean_col_names <- paste(top_headers, bottom_headers, sep = "_")
} else {
  # If it's just a normal list of headers, unlist them
  clean_col_names <- unlist(raw_headers)
}

# 6. Build the Dataframe safely
opp_shooting_by_zone <- as.data.frame(data_rows, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Force the column names to map perfectly
colnames(opp_shooting_by_zone) <- clean_col_names[1:ncol(opp_shooting_by_zone)]

# 7. Clean up the math columns 
# (Columns 1 to 5 are Name/Team info, everything 6 and beyond is stats)
opp_shooting_by_zone <- opp_shooting_by_zone %>%
  rename(PLAYER_NAME = INFO_PLAYER_NAME) %>% # Rename for easy joining later
  mutate(across(c(6:ncol(.)), as.numeric))

# Let's see the data!
View(opp_shooting_by_zone)
```

```{r}

    Right_Corner_3_FGA = `Left Corner 3_OPP_FGA`,
    Right_Corner_3_FG_PCT = `Right Corner 3_OPP_FG_PCT`,
    
    # Above the Break 3
    Above_the_Break_3_FGM = `Above the Break 3_OPP_FGM`,
    Above_the_Break_3_FGA = `Backcourt_OPP_FGA`,
    Above_the_Break_3_FG_PCT = `Corner 3_OPP_FG_PCT`,
    
    # Corner 3 Combined
    Corner_3_FGM = `Left Corner 3_OPP_FGM`,
    Corner_3_FGA = `Right Corner 3_OPP_FGA`,
    Corner_3_FG_PCT = `Above the Break 3_OPP_FG_PCT`,
    
    # Backcourt
    Backcourt_FGM = `Restricted Area_OPP_FGM`,
    Backcourt_FGA = `In The Paint (Non-RA)_OPP_FGA`,
    Backcourt_FG_PCT = `Mid-Range_OPP_FG_PCT`
  )

# Verify the fix!
View(clean_opp_shooting)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)

# 1. Build your list of dataframes
def_data_list <- list(
  ten_nba_tracking_defense,
  fifte_nba_tracking_defense,
  two_nba_tracking_defense,
  six_nba_tracking_defense,
  three_nba_tracking_defense,
  overall_nba_tracking_defense
)

# 2. Create a matching list of suffixes for those 6 dataframes
suffixes <- c("_10FT", "_15FT", "_2P", "_6FT", "_3P", "_OVERALL")

# 3. Clean AND Rename in one shot!
def_data_list_clean <- purrr::map2(def_data_list, suffixes, function(df, suffix) {
  df %>%
    # First, drop the junk columns
    select(
      -contains("TEAM"),
      -starts_with("GP"),
      -starts_with("G"),
      -starts_with("FREQ"),
      -starts_with("AGE"),
      -starts_with("CLOSE_DEF_PERSON_ID"),
      -starts_with("PLAYER_POSITION")
    ) %>%
    # Second, stick the suffix onto every remaining column EXCEPT the player's name
    rename_with(~paste0(., suffix), .cols = -PLAYER_NAME)
})

# 4. Merge the newly tagged list!
clean_defensive_tracking <- purrr::reduce(def_data_list_clean, full_join, by = "PLAYER_NAME") %>%
  # Convert everything to numbers and fill NAs with 0
  mutate(across(-PLAYER_NAME, as.numeric)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~replace_na(.x, 0)))

# Behold your final, beautifully labeled defensive matrix!
View(clean_defensive_tracking)
```


```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# The Ultimate Cleanup Pipeline
clean_defensive_tracking <- all_defensive_tracking %>%
  # 1. Drop TEAM, GP, G, and FREQ columns safely
  select(
    -contains("TEAM"),
    -starts_with("GP_"),   # Drops GP_OVERALL, GP_3P, etc.
    -starts_with("G_"),    # Drops G_OVERALL, G_3P, etc. (Safe from FGM)
    -starts_with("FREQ_")  # Drops FREQ_OVERALL, FREQ_3P, etc.
  ) %>%
  # 2. Convert all stats to numbers
  mutate(across(-PLAYER_NAME, as.numeric)) %>%
  # 3. Fill in the NAs with 0
  mutate(across(everything(), ~replace_na(.x, 0)))

# Take a look at your perfectly filtered metrics!
View(clean_defensive_tracking)
```



```{r}
#write.csv(opp_shooting_by_zone, "opp_shooting_by_zone.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(clean_defensive_tracking, "defensive_tracking.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```
